thread:
Maya: quick sync 11 are we ok with sidecar writing prefetch entries to node-local storage or should runtime own all cache writes? concerns about tenant isolation.

Drew: current branch lets sidecar write for speed, runtime write for strict routes. we hit a test where tenant scope was missed.

Aisha: saw the same. sidecar wrote into a shared path and entries were visible across tenants. compliance flagged it.

Tom: is the fix just to include tenant id in the path?

Drew: that fixes the immediate leak, but raises a design question: sidecar-as-writer vs sidecar-as-coordinator.

Maya: I'm leaning coordinator-only for safety. fewer write surfaces; runtime can validate ACLs.

Carla: coordinator-only costs RPCs. microbenchmarks show added median ~0.7-1ms and p99 regression under load. tradeoff is safety vs tail latency.

Aisha: propose HYBRID: sidecar writes to an ephemeral tenant-scoped namespace and runtime promotes atomically after validation. also require audit event on any sidecar write.

Tom: promotion must be very fast (target <1ms for memory). if it hits disk, we need per-mode defaults.

Drew: sketch config:
```
prefetch {
 mode: HYBRID
 tenant_tokens: 100
 global_concurrency: 400
 promote_timeout_ms: 10
}
```

Maya: add backpressure: token-bucket + global cap + per-node eviction TTL. label HYBRID as temporary and plan to migrate to COORDINATOR_ONLY.

infra-bot: deploy planned: prefetch-hybrid v0.1 -> canary in 1h. CI green. :rocket:

Drew: action items: Aisha add audit logging + path enforcement; Carla add token-bucket metrics; Tom run promote latency matrix (mem/tmpfs/disk); Maya draft migration flip and FF gates.

Maya: thanks, tagging owners in the doc. :thumbsup:
